correctness.rationale: For all x>0, basis vectors u_n=z^n/sqrt(n!) and v_n=z^n(n+1-|z|²)/sqrt((n+1)!) are normalized and angularly orthogonal in Gaussian L². The exact integral of d[t^(n+1)e^(-t)] produces each coefficient e^(-x)x^(n+1)/sqrt(n!(n+1)!), proving the complete positive singular-value list. Its ratio determines modes, Bessel series gives exact Hilbert–Schmidt power, monotonic b_n envelopes prove sharp strict global norm, and Poisson Stirling bounds with global exponential tails justify the uniform-in-edge-window p-power Riemann sum and fixed-threshold counts. Fixed coordinates vanish at large x while norm does not. Packaged standalone checker passed 689 finite numerical assertions; finite tests are explicitly not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The claimed new object is the full singular spectrum of the off-diagonal level-zero-to-one hard-disk compression and its universally sharp, nonattained norm plus all-fixed-exponent Gaussian spectral edge and threshold counting constants. Full-text inspection of the closest primary sources found same-level concentration eigenvalues, general polyanalytic bases/symbol calculus, Wigner zeros, and multilevel entropy traces, not a statement that implies all of the proposed cross-level formulas. Similarity searches returned related but non-dominating diagonal Fock Toeplitz and abstract weighted-shift results. This is provisional best-knowledge priority, not uniqueness or complete bibliographic certification.

value.rationale: Interlevel coupling under spatial observation is a natural multiband phase-space localization invariant, distinct from same-level occupation probabilities. It has a structurally sharp, globally nonattained universal coupling constant and a concrete spectral escape paradox (strong convergence to zero despite positive asymptotic norm). The complete singular sequence and Gaussian boundary layer supply meaningful Schatten, counting, and mode-transition laws for every fixed positive exponent, useful as a quantitative benchmark for multiband localization rather than a routine single small-case computation.
